title: subsystem_command_contract_set
description: SYS-8 of the System-Level Verification Integration workflow. OUTPUT contract for dv_harness/subsystem_command_contract.py's build_contract_set(): one SubsystemCommandContract per (command.txt, command) of every selected subsystem, plus the cross-subsystem conflicts that contract set exposes. Unlike soc_arch_map.schema.json / register_map.schema.json (which are INPUT contracts a project supplies), this document is DERIVED: every field is computed from the real command.txt files by build_contract_set(), and the source command.txt is never modified -- SYS-7's 'Do not modify command.txt during discovery' and SYS-8's 'Keep original command.txt intact' are both properties of the only code that writes this document. This is a planning/reporting artifact: it describes what a System-Level composition WOULD have to schedule and arbitrate. It is never itself a System command.txt, a command router or a virtual sequencer, and nothing downstream may auto-apply it into a real generated artifact -- that is SYS-40 and requires a separate explicit human approval.

subsystems.description: The subsystem ids this contract set covers, as supplied by the SYS-1 selection. A one-element list is legal and is exactly the case in which every contract's parallel_safe must be UNKNOWN.

command_txt_modified.description: Structural restatement of SYS-8's 'Keep original command.txt intact'. The value is a const rather than a boolean: a document claiming a command.txt was modified is not a valid document of this schema, because no code path in this module can produce one.

phase_boundary.description: The SYS-39 stop condition carried on the artifact itself, so a reader of the file alone knows this is analysis and not an implementation authorization.

conflicts.description: CROSS-SUBSYSTEM conflicts only. Contention inside one subsystem's own sequential command.txt is ordinary and is expressed by ordering_constraints, not reported here.

evidence_list.description: Real citations, each '<file>:<line>' against the unmodified source command.txt so any claim in this document can be checked at its origin.

contract.description: SYS-8's own field list, verbatim and in its own order, plus parallel_safety_reason. The field list is held to dv_harness/subsystem_command_contract.py's SYS8_FIELDS by a test, so the requirement, the dataclass and this schema cannot drift apart.

source_command_file.description: Path of the real command.txt this contract was derived from. Read-only input.

command_name.description: The macro / model-task / system-task name as it is actually written in the file (e.g. 'HOSTWRITE4B', '`SMEMMODEL.FILLMEM'), never a normalised or invented name.

command_category.description: SYS-7's init/config/traffic wording made derivable. A register access is REGISTER_ACCESS and is deliberately NOT split into config-vs-traffic: nothing in the file states which it is, and a guess would be fabricated evidence.

arguments.description: Positional argument profile across every invocation. role is derived from the macro SHAPE (position 0 of a register access is the ADDRESS), never from the value.

target_agent.description: The agent/handler that executes this command. Derived from the macro prefix's HOST/CPU/DEV convention, or taken from a declared command_inventory.csv HANDLER when the project has recorded one. 'UNKNOWN' when neither source answers.

target_vip.description: The VIP/model instance whose task is invoked. 'UNKNOWN' for a raw register macro, which names no VIP.

target_sequence.description: The invoked task/sequence name, or a declared command_inventory.csv VIP_SEQUENCE. Empty when the file names none -- empty is a fact here, not a placeholder.

required_resources.description: Prefixed resource ids (REGISTER_BLOCK / BFM / MODEL / MEMORY_MODEL / HIERARCHY) so SYS-9's inventory and SYS-10's duplicate detection can compare two subsystems by string equality rather than by class name -- SYS-10's own 'Do not decide duplicates by class names alone'.

access.description: WRITE means this command actively drives the resource. Two subsystems both READING one resource is not a driver conflict and is not reported as one.

basis.description: What in the statement made this resource visible, so the derivation is checkable.

ordering_constraints.description: This command's view of the SYS-7 ordering edges computed once per file by reference_pattern_audit.build_ordering_constraints(). Identical repeated edges are collapsed with an occurrences count -- 900 copies of one fact is not more evidence than one copy plus a number.

clock_domain.description: Two-step resolution: the command's addresses are located in the project's real address map, then mapped to a clock through a declared region->clock mapping. Each step can honestly fail: a soc_arch_map address_map entry carries no clock of its own, so UNRESOLVED naming the located regions is the correct answer without a declared mapping, and is the input SYS-29's cross-subsystem clock-domain comparison will consume.

basis.description: Name-token evidence, and it says so. A register write whose trailing comment reads '//usb ctrl rst=1' is real evidence of reset involvement and is not proof; the matched token is carried so a reader can judge it.

shared_resource_dependency.description: Resources this command needs that a DIFFERENT subsystem's command also needs. Empty in a single-subsystem set by construction.

parallel_safe.description: Whether this command may run concurrently with ANOTHER SUBSYSTEM's commands. Three-valued on purpose: a contract set holding one subsystem has no second subsystem to be concurrent with and must report UNKNOWN rather than a verdict nothing supports.

parallel_safety_reason.description: Why parallel_safe holds that value. Required in practice for the UNKNOWN case, where the reason is the entire content of the verdict.

condition_list.description: Order-based, not causal: a command.txt's own text can support 'this initialization call appears before every invocation of this command' and cannot support 'this command requires it'. Each entry cites the line it was read from.

conflict_type.description: DUPLICATE_ACTIVE_DRIVER is the 'PCIe and USB both contain a CPU AXI Master' shape SYS-10/SYS-12 exist for; its resolution is SYS-12's own rule -- stop automatic integration of that resource until ownership is resolved.

resolution.description: A statement of what must happen next, never an action this module takes. Deciding the relationship is SYS-11..SYS-13; implementing a shared agent is SYS-40 and requires a separate explicit human approval.
